correctness.rationale: A complete finite graph-and-face enumeration gives 24 perfect matchings and 20,977 nonempty faces for each of three rotational edge representatives. Exhaustive topological sorting proves that the three gradient matchings are acyclic; critical cells are one vertex, no one-cells, and (4,8), (5,9), (7,11) two/three-cells. Exact signed Morse boundaries have nonzero Smith diagonals 1,...,1,2, giving M(Z/2,2) wedged with four three-spheres by the homotopy classification of two/three-cell attachments. Explicit eight-triangle cycles are nonzero in mod-two H2 for each fault and remain nonboundaries in the original intact simplicial boundary, so by UCT and the integral Smith groups the inclusion on Z/2 is an isomorphism. All 30 edges are covered by the cyclic rotations of three types. The complete code was executed from the actual packaged source.

value.rationale: The dodecahedron is a canonical symmetric polyhedral graph and its intact perfect-matching complex has a rare order-two Moore summand. Determining whether this integral torsion survives one arbitrary edge fault is a motivated fault-robustness question. The result determines the full faulty integral homotopy type and the nonzero torsion inclusion, neither inferable from the intact homotopy type or matching counts. It is not an arbitrary small parameter increment or an isolated numerical rank, and it provides an exact benchmark for matching-topology robustness.
